goal: Show whether the six naviquest tools answer real research questions more cheaply than a competent fetch-and-read agent, at no cost in answer quality.

primary_kpi.name: tokens_per_answered_task
primary_kpi.estimator: chars/4 of the full result JSON, charged identically to both arms

secondary_kpis.name: context_held
secondary_kpis.note: largest single payload the agent must keep resident

secondary_kpis.name: wall_clock
secondary_kpis.note: reported, not optimized — the baseline can legitimately win this

environment.note: Chrome, launch flags, SDK injection, CDP/WebMCP transport, persistent sessions, reader settlement, and model warm-up are the skill host's contract, not this eval's. This file does not restate them.
environment.ai_mode_requires_when_on: the skill warms the Chrome profile first; the harness then requires LanguageModel=available on the exact opened page before a measured tool call
environment.reader_settling: the skill host settles the page reader; retries count toward wall-clock and only the settled payload is charged to agent-visible tokens

budget.network_calls: unbounded — this eval is deliberately live; it is not a gate

decision_rule: ACCEPT the retrieval claim when naviquest's tokens_per_answered_task and context_held are materially below the baseline's, the blind judge shows no quality regression, and every guardrail holds. A wall-clock loss does not block acceptance; an unstated AI_MODE does.
